what: Angle between the direction the physics engine gives for the Sun and the Earth and the direction NASA's JPL Horizons System gives, for the same site and hour.
changes_from_version_1: 17 preset sites instead of 3; every hour of a whole year instead of 30 days; one sample per week stored as rows under fixed columns; statistics to 1e-6 degree; retrieval time and query kept per site and body; heights recorded per site with their source.

signature_of_first_answer.ephemeris_line: Ephemeris / API_USER Sun Nov 15 06:01:26 2026 Pasadena, USA      / Horizons

engine.positions: app.physics.engine.positions (MOON_ME, km, geometric, aberration correction NONE)

statistics: max_deg, p95_deg (value at rank 0.95 * (n - 1), rounded down) and mean_deg over every sample: the angle on the sky between the two directions, and the absolute difference in elevation.
expected_differences: Horizons corrects for light time and stellar aberration and the engine's positions are geometric; Horizons uses its own lunar body-fixed frame. Small differences are expected. Terrain is not part of this check.
